sections.heading: C2 — KG hints for Traffic Control Device Categories and Pavement Markings
sections.markdown:
## C2 — KG hints for Traffic Control Device Categories and Pavement Markings

FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A01
A broken yellow centerline may be crossed to pass when safe, while a solid yellow no passing line may be crossed only for a left turn into or out of an alley, private road or driveway [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint yellow-lines; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec07-F06 and sec07-F08.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A02
A single solid white line may be crossed only in unusual circumstances with great care, while a double solid white line may never be crossed [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint white-lines; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec07-F11 and sec07-F12.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A01
Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, while white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint line-colors; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec07-F05 and sec07-F09.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec07-R04 | anchor: A04
White obstruction markings may be passed on either side, while yellow obstruction markings must be passed on the right only [A04].
Why it matters: group_hint obstruction-markings; prereq_hint sec07-R03; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec07-F19 and sec07-F18.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec07-R05 | anchor: A03
The two-way left turn lane is open to vehicles from both directions for left turns only, while double solid yellow lines without such a lane allow crossing only for a left turn into a driveway or alley [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint yellow-lines; prereq_hint sec07-R01; difficulty_hint two; confusable_with sec07-F17 and sec07-F07.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec07-R06 | anchor: A03
A stop line marks the exact stopping place at an intersection or crosswalk, while crosswalk lines mark where pedestrians cross and oblige drivers to stop for them [A03].
Why it matters: group_hint stop-and-crosswalk; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec07-F15 and sec07-F16.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec07-R07 | anchor: A02
White edge lines run along the right edge of the roadway, while yellow edge lines may run along the left edge of a divided highway [A02].
Why it matters: group_hint line-colors; prereq_hint sec07-R03; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec07-F14 and sec07-F13.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec07-R08 | anchor: A04
A single directional arrow commands one movement only, while a lane with arrows for more than one direction lets you choose any of those directions [A04].
Why it matters: group_hint directional-markings; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec07-F20 and sec07-F09.
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec07-R09 | anchor: A05
Railroad crossing pavement markings are white with a yellow no-passing centerline, while red pavement markings mean a roadway must not be entered at all [A05].
Why it matters: group_hint special-markings; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec07-F21 and sec07-F13.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec07-R10 | anchor: A01
A regulatory device requires an action and carries a penalty for non-compliance, while a warning device advises of a hazard and ignoring it risks a crash through negligence [A01].
Why it matters: group_hint device-categories; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec07-F02 and sec07-F03.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec07-R11 | anchor: A05
A traffic island directs vehicles into separate lanes, while a safety island is a traffic island that shelters pedestrians, and neither may be driven into or across [A05].
Why it matters: group_hint islands; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint one; confusable_with sec07-F22 and sec07-F23.
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-hi-x:hawaii-department-of-transportation-hdot:handbook:pdf-0038]
